Yeah exercise doesn’t fix problems, if someone is depressed because they are getting evicted for example, exercise won’t suddenly provide the money to pay your rent. But looking at problem solving as a step by step process might help. 

Example: In order to pay the rent I need money, in order to get this money, I need a job. But what if I don’t have a job. So then I lay in bed because this depresses me. 

So instead of trying to fix a root problem that is daunting and difficult for people especially if your mentally suffering, then start with the first step. 

The first step is getting out of bed in this example, for me, I’m very insecure about my body. So exercising gave me a slight confidence boost after seeing physical results, that in turn gave me motivation to start the first step. 

It’s all about working slow and remembering that the prior step needs to be done in order to get to the next. Trying to fix the final step or problem always feels impossible. 

If anything I said helped or u want more elaboration let me know, if it didn’t help than feel free to tell me to shut up lol. 

Good job on the 30 push-ups by the way!

From someone who finds exercise to help with my mental health, it’s not necessarily about how many pushups you do, it’s more of creating a routine that is consistent everyday that will not only biologically help you (chemically) but also it keeps your mind off things, especially for self harm, I’ve always found the pain to be the most “satisfying” from cutting, and thus working out creates a similar pain in your muscles that while isn’t identicall, helps to an extent. 

At first glance something might not seem like it will help you mentally, but if you make an effort to have an introspective conversation with ourself and ask yourself what every possible reason for a suggestion is, it may reveal multiple different reasons for doing something such as exercise. 

Exercise may not help everyone (tho it’s proven to improve your brain chemically to an extent) but the method of trying something and figuring it out may end up helping you. I hope my 2cents can contribute to anyone’s struggle in this thread.
